changes: Verified every plan number by script: the LSTM step (0.8808, 0.7616, 1.2616, 0.4258), the forget-bias memory table, the parameter counts (4,480; 8,448; 12,961; 3,360; 141,312), the leaky-integrator half-life of 6.58 steps, padding at 38%, MASE 1.22 and 0.30. All match the plan.

Ran the source forecaster exactly as published. It gives LSTM 1.075 against naive 0.155, training inputs spanning -1.92..1.92 and test inputs 1.46..3.10, mean error -0.87, and linear AR 0.099, which confirms the plan. The per-window-normalised LSTM gave 0.139 and 0.121 on two seeds with my seeding (the plan says 0.126-0.137 over three seeds). The text says 'about 0.12 to 0.14, depending on the seed'.

Overlap worked example: the plan's 'almost every test window' is now quantified. About 96% of test windows have a neighbour sharing 63 values in training (1 - 0.2^2), and 0.2^4 = 0.0016 is the chance that none of the four nearest windows is in training. Note that the source's actual split gives 2,936/936 windows, not 3,000; the 3,000 in the example is hypothetical, as the plan has it.
Added an exact form the plan did not give: the time constant 1/(1-f) of the forget gate is 1 + e^{b_f}. This motivates chrono initialisation's b_f ≈ ln(T-1).

Recursive and direct linear forecasts are described as 'nearly coincide', not 'coincide', with the reason (the window holds the whole linear state). This hedges the plan's 'identical numbers' in case Lab 3's last digits differ.

Weiss et al.: the claim is attributed with the explanation that the LSTM's unbounded cell can count while the GRU's state interpolates between bounded values. Karpathy et al.: I kept only line position and quotation tracking and dropped bracket depth, because I could not confirm it.
